l2-input.plainEnglish: Hold the aim button and a second input layer swaps what the other buttons mean. The use graph still starts when its action fires. The layer never puts a trace on Tick.
l2-input.whyGame: Players expect the same Interact event after they rebind a paddle. If the layer is implemented as a Tick that reads raw keys, every new pad layout becomes a code change.

expansions.title: Radial menu
expansions.detail: While the layer is held, a face button can open a radial. Releasing the layer returns that button to fire.

expansions.title: Ping
expansions.detail: Ping can be a third action on the same layer. It does not replace the use trace.

expansions.title: Hold versus tap
expansions.detail: A tap can stay on the base context. Only the hold pushes the L2 layer.

quiz.prompt: Holding the aim button swaps which actions the other buttons fire. What still starts the use trace?
choices: Whatever action the active layer bound, through its Triggered pin
A poll of the keyboard inside Tick
The radial widget deciding the trace origin
quiz.why: Layers remap actions. They do not replace the event.

quiz.prompt: Graph_IA_Interact_tpl_interact_input still appears under the L2 layer. What did not change?
choices: The function still means the player asked for a use
The function now means the barrel heated up
The function now loads the save slot
quiz.why: Same action, possibly a different physical button.

quiz.prompt: The radial menu opens from the layer. Which node must not move onto the use trace to build that menu?
choices: A widget spawn, which is the menu's job rather than the look's job
The interface call on a hit. That call is use, not the modifier layer.
quiz.why: The look reports a hit. The menu is another action.

quiz.prompt: Someone reads the raw gamepad button inside Tick whenever the layer might be held. What breaks on a new controller layout?
choices: The code names a button that the new layout moved
quiz.why: The mapping context is how layouts change without code.

quiz.prompt: A player taps the button instead of holding it. The base context still has fire. What should happen?
choices: Fire runs. The L2 layer never pushed
The use trace runs because any press is use
quiz.why: Hold pushes the layer. Tap does not.

quiz.prompt: Where does the extra mapping context get added while aiming?
choices: On the possessed pawn or the player controller, for the hold
Inside OnRep of EquippedId. The notify shows the equipped weapon. It does not open the radial layer.
quiz.why: The same owner as the base context.

quiz.prompt: True or false: an input layer may remap a button without moving the use trace onto Tick.
quiz.why: Remap the action. Keep the event.

quiz.prompt: The radial menu is opened by the modifier-layer action, not by the line trace.
quiz.why: The true pin calls Interact. The menu is its own action.

quiz.prompt: A streamer rebinds the layer to a back paddle. Which asset do they edit?
choices: The mapping context for that hold
The limb clamp at ten percent
quiz.why: Bindings live in the context.

quiz.prompt: Releasing the aim hold should pop the L2 mapping context.
quiz.why: Releasing the hold pops the layer.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does holding aim swap a second input layer instead of reading raw keys on Tick?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What breaks after a paddle rebind if that layer is a Tick reading key codes?

gasp.plainEnglish: Motion matching plays the run or the walk by reading Speed. This graph's only job is to write Speed when the stick changes. It does not sample animation curves.
gasp.whyGame: If the anim graph also writes Speed, the stick and the pose fight. If Tick writes 600 whenever the menu is open, motion matching plays a sprint during a buy phase.

expansions.title: Strafe
expansions.detail: A sideways pose can read the same Speed plus an axis sign. It should not add a second writer.

expansions.title: Stop
expansions.detail: Releasing the stick writes the walk or zero. The stop pose is chosen from that number.

expansions.title: Crouch blend
expansions.detail: Crouch can be another float the matcher reads. The move action still owns Speed.

quiz.prompt: Motion matching needs a gait. What does this graph actually store?
choices: Speed, from the stick, for the matcher to read
quiz.why: The graph writes the number. The matcher plays the pose.

quiz.prompt: Speed = 600.f sits on the true side of the move branch. When is that line correct?
choices: When the axis is greater than zero
When the pawn is in a menu
When a limb hit was clamped
quiz.why: Pushed stick, sprint number.

quiz.prompt: The animation blueprint wants to write Speed from the current pose. What loop does that create?
choices: The pose and the stick overwrite each other
A cleaner gait, because the pose knows best
quiz.why: One writer. The matcher is a reader.

quiz.prompt: Tick forces Speed = 600 during a buy menu. What does motion matching play?
choices: A sprint, even though the stick is idle
A correct idle, because Tick is ignored by the matcher
Menus are assumed to freeze the gait number
quiz.why: The matcher believes the number.

quiz.prompt: The false path writes 200. A player eases off the stick mid-stride. Which pose should be allowed to start?
choices: The sprint, until the magazine is empty
quiz.why: Released axis selects the walk literal.

quiz.prompt: Where should a designer change 600 and 200 without touching the anim graph?
choices: In the literals or a data row the move function reads
quiz.why: The number is gameplay data. The matcher only reads it.

quiz.prompt: True or false: motion matching should read Speed rather than write it.
quiz.why: The stick owns the write.

quiz.prompt: Speed is written by the move graph, and the pose is chosen from that speed.
quiz.why: That inverts reader and writer.

quiz.prompt: A stance system sets Speed to 120 while aiming. The move graph then ticks. What survives?
choices: Only if the move graph is not on Tick. Otherwise 600 or 200 replaces 120
The stance speed survives because frames respect other writers
The two writers cancel and the pawn stops
quiz.why: Tick stomps the stance.

quiz.prompt: True or false: Graph_IA_Move is still the function that chooses 600 or 200.
quiz.why: Motion matching did not replace that function.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why may this graph write Speed only when the stick changes?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What fight starts if the anim graph and Tick both write Speed?

aoi.plainEnglish: About twice a second the server traces and stores whether this actor is still relevant. Clients do not set that bit, and fog's Visible flag is a different fact.
aoi.whyGame: Forcing Relevant true from Tick keeps every distant rifle replicating. Copying Visible into Relevant hides people who are in fog but still close enough to matter, or the reverse.

expansions.title: Squad exception
expansions.detail: Squadmates can stay relevant without a hit. That exception is still decided on the server timer, not on Tick.

expansions.title: Vehicle
expansions.detail: A vehicle can use a larger radius on the same CheckAOI pass.

expansions.title: Dormancy
expansions.detail: A failed interest check can allow dormancy. The fog bit must not be the switch.

quiz.prompt: Relevant is decided how often in this lesson?
choices: On a timer of about half a second
quiz.why: CheckAOI is scheduled at 0.5 seconds.

quiz.prompt: Relevant = bHit stores the interest trace. What must that line not copy instead?
choices: How many rounds the reload wants
quiz.why: Fog and relevance answer different questions.

quiz.prompt: Begin Play in the AOI graph arms a timer. What runs when that timer fires?
choices: CheckAOI, which traces and may set Relevant
quiz.why: The timer is the schedule. CheckAOI is the pass.

quiz.prompt: Tick sets Relevant true for every rifle. What does the listen server keep paying for?
choices: Replication of pawns that failed the interest test
quiz.why: True means keep replicating.

quiz.prompt: A client marks itself relevant so it cannot be culled. Where is that refused?
choices: On the server, because HasAuthority wraps the write
quiz.why: Relevance is a server decision.

quiz.prompt: A teammate is in fog but standing next to you. Which bit can still be true?
choices: Relevant, even though Visible is false
Neither flag can be set if they are secretly one bool
Visible only, because fog implies distance
Standing close should warm the barrel instead
quiz.why: You can be near and unseen.

quiz.prompt: True or false: CheckAOI should run from a timer rather than from Tick.
quiz.why: Half a second is the lesson's clock.

quiz.prompt: Visible says who may see a cell, and Relevant says who receives the actor.
quiz.why: Sight and network interest differ.

quiz.prompt: The interest trace misses. What should Relevant become?
choices: Forcing everyone to stay replicated so models never vanish
quiz.why: The line stores the hit result, not a constant true.

quiz.prompt: True or false: a client may set Relevant so their kill still replicates.
quiz.why: The server decides who still matters.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does the server trace about twice a second to store relevance?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What keeps replicating if Relevant is forced true from Tick for a distant rifle?

ballistics.plainEnglish: One press of fire traces once. A hit adds a small step of heat. Aiming, by itself, does not warm the barrel, and wear can read that heat later.
ballistics.whyGame: Adding 0.05 heat from Tick while the player merely aims cooks the gun in a standoff. Tracing again from the anim blueprint rediscovers a target the fire event already named.

expansions.title: Wear
expansions.detail: Wear can accumulate from Heat on the same hit. It should not have its own Tick.

expansions.title: Spread
expansions.detail: Spread can read Heat to widen the next trace. The trace still starts at IA_Fire.

expansions.title: Cooling
expansions.detail: Cooling is a timer after the last shot, not a per-frame subtract while aiming.

quiz.prompt: A shot traces once and then may heat the barrel. Which action starts that trace?
quiz.why: Aiming is not firing.

quiz.prompt: Heat = Heat + 0.05f runs on a hit. What does the player feel if it also runs while they only aim?
choices: The barrel climbs during a standoff with no shot
quiz.why: Heat belongs to the shot.

quiz.prompt: The trace hits. Which node gates the heat write?
choices: Branch on the hit bool, before Set Heat
quiz.why: A miss does not warm the barrel in this excerpt.

quiz.prompt: The animation blueprint traces again to decide recoil. What does it rediscover?
choices: A target the fire event already had
A cheaper answer than the fire trace
quiz.why: One trace per shot is the budget.

quiz.prompt: Wear is state on the weapon. What should it read instead of ticking?
quiz.why: Wear follows heat. It does not poll.

quiz.prompt: A miss is fired. Does this excerpt add 0.05 heat?
choices: No. The branch skips Set Heat
Every trigger press should warm the barrel even on a miss
quiz.why: The true pin is the hit.

quiz.prompt: True or false: IA_Fire is the start of the ballistics trace.
quiz.why: The function is the fire action.

quiz.prompt: True or false: aiming alone should add the same 0.05 heat as a hit.
quiz.why: Aim is a different action.

quiz.prompt: Cooling the barrel by subtracting heat every frame fights which later design?
choices: A timer that starts after the last shot
quiz.why: Cooling is a clock, not a frame tax.

quiz.prompt: True or false: Graph_IA_Fire should run from Tick so heat stays smooth.
quiz.why: Fire is a press.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does one fire press trace once and add heat, while aiming alone stays cold?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What cooks the barrel if heat climbs from Tick during a standoff?

limbs.plainEnglish: A normal hit may hurt a limb, but the authority will not take that limb below ten percent of its max. The server writes the float. OnRep plays the limp and does not subtract again.
limbs.whyGame: Without the floor, one unlucky hit deletes the limb and the death state never matches the design. A client that writes the limb desyncs the limp from the server.

expansions.title: Bleed
expansions.detail: Bleed can be a timer after the limb is wounded. It still starts from the authority's number.

expansions.title: Splint
expansions.detail: A splint item can raise the limb through the same authority write, not through the widget.

expansions.title: Downed arm
expansions.detail: Below the floor you need a special hit, not a second Tick.

quiz.prompt: A normal hit must not drop a limb below ten percent. Who enforces that floor?
choices: The authority, when it writes the limb float
quiz.why: The server owns the float and the clamp.

quiz.prompt: Health = 90 is the sample write after a hit that would have gone lower. What is that line protecting?
choices: The ten-percent floor on a limb whose max is 100
quiz.why: 90 is the floor in the sample, not a random heal.

quiz.prompt: OnRep plays the limp. What must it refuse to do with the limb float?
quiz.why: The authority already applied the floor.

quiz.prompt: Tick writes the limb from 100 straight toward zero. What design dies?
choices: The rule that a normal hit cannot erase the limb
quiz.why: Tick ignores the floor and the damage event.

quiz.prompt: A special execution is allowed to pass the floor. Where is that exception decided?
choices: On the authority, in the damage path, not on the proxy
quiz.why: Exceptions are still server rules.

quiz.prompt: The HUD shows a limb at 10 while the server has 40. What likely wrote the widget's number?
choices: The client, instead of waiting for replication
The interest pass writing into the limb bar
quiz.why: The bar must read the replicated float.

quiz.prompt: True or false: a normal limb hit is floored by the authority, not by OnRep.
quiz.why: OnRep plays the result.

quiz.prompt: True or false: OnRep should clamp the limb again in case the server forgot.
quiz.why: A second clamp hides a server bug and can still double-apply.

quiz.prompt: Bleed damage over time is added. What schedule matches this lesson?
choices: A timer the authority starts after the wound
quiz.why: Another clock, still not a frame, still the server.

quiz.prompt: True or false: proxies may lower a limb so the limp starts before the server replies.
quiz.why: They can play a guess only if they do not own the float.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why will the authority not take a limb below ten percent of its max on a normal hit?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What death state fails if one unlucky hit is allowed to delete the limb?

inventory.plainEnglish: Overlap asks AddToSlot through the interface. The slot owns the count. A use trace that also increments the stack will fill the bag by looking.
inventory.whyGame: Intermediate kits add more item types. If each type gets its own overlap function that also knows about magazines and limbs, every new item edits three systems.

expansions.title: Armor plate
expansions.detail: A plate can be another slot id. Overlap still only asks.

expansions.title: Drop
expansions.detail: Drop decrements the slot on the authority and spawns a pickup. It is not a trace.

expansions.title: Stack cap
expansions.detail: The cap can live on the item row. The overlap does not hard-code it.

quiz.prompt: Overlap asks the interface and the slot owns the count. Which function is the ask?
choices: AddToSlot, via ProcessEvent on the overlapping actor
quiz.why: The interface keeps item types out of the overlap.

quiz.prompt: StackCount is cleared after a successful add. What bug appears if the clear happens first?
choices: A refused add still destroys the offered stack
quiz.why: Clear only after the slot accepts.

quiz.prompt: The branch in front of AddToSlot checks StackCount > 0. What walks in with zero?
choices: An empty overlap that must not invent an item
quiz.why: Zero means nothing to give.

quiz.prompt: The use trace adds one to the stack when it hits a crate. What did the player not have to do?
quiz.why: Looking is not picking up.

quiz.prompt: Plates, keys, and ammo all want this pattern. What stays out of the overlap function?
choices: The per-item rules, which live behind AddToSlot
quiz.why: The ask is generic. The slot is specific.

quiz.prompt: A full slot refuses a plate. The pickup then destroys itself. What was lost?
choices: The plate, because a refusal is not a transfer
A refusal still counts as a successful move
quiz.why: Destroy only after success.

quiz.prompt: True or false: the inventory overlap should call AddToSlot rather than edit the count inline.
quiz.why: The slot owns the number.

quiz.prompt: True or false: a use-trace hit is a successful pickup in this lesson.
quiz.why: Use is Interact. Pickup is overlap.

quiz.prompt: Dropping a plate should spawn a pickup and decrement the slot. Who writes the decrement?
quiz.why: The slot still owns the count.

quiz.prompt: True or false: each item type needs its own overlap graph.
quiz.why: One ask, many slot ids.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does overlap call AddToSlot while a use trace must not also increment the stack?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What happens to magazines and limbs if every new item type grows its own overlap function?

gunsmith.plainEnglish: Ten weapon definitions live in data. Equipping writes EquippedId on the authority. Everyone else builds the third-person mesh from that id.
gunsmith.whyGame: A client that sets EquippedId directly pops weapons the server never granted. Replicating ten meshes every equip wastes bandwidth the id would have saved.

expansions.title: Locked slot
expansions.detail: The authority rejects an id the inventory does not contain.

expansions.title: Charm
expansions.detail: A charm can be another id on the same row, still not a replicated mesh.

expansions.title: Inspect
expansions.detail: Inspect is a montage local to the owner. It does not change EquippedId.

quiz.prompt: Ten slots stay in the data asset. What replicates when you equip one?
quiz.why: The id selects a local asset.

quiz.prompt: EquippedId = IA_Equip is outside HasAuthority in a broken sample. What do proxies show?
choices: A weapon the server did not agree to
The correct server weapon, because clients are ignored
quiz.why: The write skipped the gate.

quiz.prompt: Before the id changes, which check has to pass?
quiz.why: Shared id, authority write.

quiz.prompt: A data row holds mesh, mag size, and damage for slot 4. A remote player receives id 4. What do they load locally?
choices: A replicated copy of the designer's unsaved file
quiz.why: The row is content. The id is the reference.

quiz.prompt: Inspect plays a montage. Should it write EquippedId?
choices: No. Inspect does not change which weapon is equipped
The inspect montage should change which gun is equipped
Inspect should clear the equipped id
quiz.why: Inspect is cosmetic on the current id.

quiz.prompt: The server rejects an id the bag does not contain. Where does that rejection live?
choices: In the authority path, before the assignment
quiz.why: The server owns the grant.

quiz.prompt: True or false: EquippedId is the replicated fact for a ten-slot gunsmith.
quiz.why: The slots stay in data.

quiz.prompt: True or false: each of the ten meshes should replicate on every equip.
quiz.why: That is the cost the id avoids.

quiz.prompt: OnRep of the id swaps the mesh. Writing a different id there would do what?
choices: Fight the server's choice on the next replication
Move rounds from reserve into the gun
An inspect should start an interest trace
quiz.why: OnRep shows the id. It does not pick a new one.

quiz.prompt: True or false: Graph_IA_Equip is the equip request in this lesson.
quiz.why: The function is the action.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why do ten weapon definitions live in data while equip only replicates EquippedId?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What pops on other machines if a client sets EquippedId to a weapon the server never granted?

save.plainEnglish: Begin Play loads one struct: the kit you actually saved. Tick does not write that struct, and loading does not replay every shot that produced the numbers.
save.whyGame: A Tick save catches heat mid-climb and a limb mid-bleed. A constructor load runs before the component can apply EquippedId, Health, and ammo.

expansions.title: Checkpoint
expansions.detail: The volume calls the same struct write as the menu.

expansions.title: Continue
expansions.detail: Continue is that Begin Play load.

expansions.title: Wipe
expansions.detail: Wipe deletes the slot object. It does not Tick the fields to zero.

quiz.prompt: Begin Play loads one struct. Which fields belong in it for this kit?
quiz.why: Save the facts the other lessons own. Not the pose.

quiz.prompt: Graph_BeginPlay_tpl_saveload_begin applies the slot. What should it not resimulate?
choices: Every shot that produced the saved heat
quiz.why: Load applies results.

quiz.prompt: Make Struct then Set SlotValue. What is the Set doing?
choices: Storing the packed snapshot on the slot
quiz.why: The struct is the snapshot. Set keeps it.

quiz.prompt: Tick writes the slot from the live limb. Why is that a bad checkpoint?
choices: The limb may still be bleeding
Heat cannot be saved any other way
quiz.why: Save a finished event.

quiz.prompt: Loading during the constructor misses EquippedId. Why?
choices: The component that applies the id is not ready yet
Constructors are server-only and saves are client-only
Ids cannot be stored in structs
quiz.why: Begin Play is late enough.

quiz.prompt: The pause menu and a checkpoint both save. How do they avoid two shapes?
choices: They each Tick a private float
quiz.why: One struct.

quiz.prompt: True or false: this lesson's load runs from Begin Play, not from Tick.
quiz.why: Begin Play applies the slot.

quiz.prompt: True or false: the saved pose of the motion-matching graph belongs in the same struct as the equipped id.
quiz.why: The pose is derived. The id is a fact.

quiz.prompt: Continue should restore a limb at 40, not replay the hit that made it 40. Which path is that?
choices: Apply the float from the struct
Fire Any Damage with the original amount
Run OnRep as if it were the authority
Add 0.05 heat until the numbers match
quiz.why: The result is the save.

quiz.prompt: True or false: SlotValue written from Tick is a finished checkpoint.
quiz.why: Tick does not know that an event finished.

assignment.plainPrompt: Why does Begin Play load the saved kit instead of Tick writing that struct?
assignment.whyGamePrompt: What half-finished numbers get stored if Tick saves heat mid-climb and a limb mid-bleed?

fps-intermediate-e5: The aim hold should write the sprint literal
A limb floor of ten percent should pick the gait
fps-intermediate-e7: Leaving every rifle relevant is cheaper than a timer
Fog's visible flag should be copied into relevance
The radial menu should decide who replicates
fps-intermediate-e11: The stick axis should start the limb write
Spawn should be the only time a limb changes
Heat rising should lower the limb
fps-intermediate-e12: Playing the limp requires subtracting again
The notify should refill the magazine
The notify should set the equipped id
fps-intermediate-e15: Clients equip faster if they write the id first
The widget is the right place to store the id
Motion matching should pick the equipped weapon
fps-intermediate-e17: A frame is a safe moment to snapshot heat
The constructor is early enough to apply the id
Relevance should be stored in the save slot
fps-intermediate-e24: Aiming should be what starts the shot trace
The interest timer should add heat
The reload key should trace the shot
fps-intermediate-e26: Smoothing heat across frames is more important than tying it to a hit
The walk speed function should add heat
OnRep of health should add the 0.05

exam.prompt: Aim is held, so the L2 layer is up, and the player taps fire. Which event adds heat?
choices: IA_Fire, and only if the shot hits
The interest timer that culls distant rifles

exam.prompt: Motion matching plays a sprint in the buy menu. Which write is lying?
True or false: Visible can stand in for Relevant when culling rifles.
exam.why: A nearby unseen player still matters.

exam.prompt: A limb shows 0 on a proxy and 90 on the server after one normal hit. What did the proxy do?
choices: It wrote the limb instead of waiting for the floored value

exam.prompt: Looking at an ammo crate increases the stack. Which wire is extra?
choices: The use trace calling the stack increment
The branch on a positive count

exam.prompt: True or false: ten gunsmith meshes should replicate instead of EquippedId.
exam.why: The id is the replicated fact.

exam.prompt: Continue restores heat at 0.4 without replaying the shots. Which function applies that?
choices: The Begin Play load of the slot

exam.prompt: A back paddle is bound to the aim hold. What asset changed?
choices: The function that traces a shot

exam.prompt: True or false: the pose graph may write Speed if the stick also writes it.
Relevant is false and Visible is true. Can that pair be honest?
choices: Yes. You can be seen by the rules of fog and still be out of network range
They are one shared bit, not two resources

exam.prompt: Which function is the interest pass?
True or false: a hit from IA_Fire may add 0.05 heat.
The authority floors a limb at 90 on a max of 100. A proxy OnRep subtracts the raw damage. What does the next replicate do?
exam.why: The server value wins. The extra subtract was local.

exam.prompt: AddToSlot is refused. The pickup is destroyed anyway. What should have happened?
choices: The pickup stays, because the slot did not take the stack
The stack is deleted on purpose

exam.prompt: True or false: a client may equip any id and the server should copy it.
Which of these belongs in the save struct?
exam.why: Save facts, not derived poses or hardware.

exam.prompt: Releasing the aim hold should pop which input object?
True or false: CheckAOI's timer is about half a second.
Wear accumulates. What should it follow?
choices: Whether the team can see you
exam.why: Wear is a reader of heat.

exam.prompt: A normal hit would compute 40 on a limb whose floor is 90. What is stored?
exam.why: The floor wins for a normal hit.

exam.prompt: True or false: the overlap graph should inline every item's rules.
exam.why: AddToSlot keeps the rules with the slot.

exam.prompt: Remote players build your gun from data. What did they receive?
choices: The buttons you bound on the pad

exam.prompt: Graph_IA_Move writes 200. What is the stick doing?
choices: An idle stick crashes the move function
exam.why: The false path is the walk literal.

exam.prompt: True or false: loading the kit in the constructor is early enough for EquippedId.
A standoff never fires, but heat climbs. Which line is running too often?
choices: The authority floor on a limb
The layer pop on aim release

exam.prompt: Who may set Relevant?
choices: The server, inside the interest pass
Any client who wants to stay replicated

exam.prompt: True or false: a miss still adds heat in the ballistics excerpt.
The bag lacks slot 9, but a client asks to equip it. What stores EquippedId?
choices: Nothing. The authority refuses before the assignment
The forbidden slot number because the client requested it
Zero written by the weapon icon

exam.prompt: Why keep limbs, heat, ammo, and the equipped id in one struct?
choices: So continue cannot mix a new gun with an old magazine
Because structs hold only one field

exam.prompt: True or false: the radial menu belongs on the use trace's true pin.
StackCount is 0 on overlap. AddToSlot should do what?
Which schedule matches Sense's idea if you were borrowing it for cooling the barrel?
choices: A timer after the last shot
Tick while the aim layer is held
